insights.title: Your kidney function is reduced, and your urine carries a lot of albumin
insights.found: On 9 Oct 2026 your eGFR was 41 mL/min/1.73 m2 (creatinine 1.82 mg/dL) and your urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio was 420 mg/g.
insights.why: Both are well outside the laboratory's ranges: eGFR 90 or more, urine albumin below 30.
insights.means: An eGFR of 41 places kidney function in stage G3b. Our rule library could source this boundary only from a guideline written for people with diabetes, and your record codes no diabetes, so the finding is informational and asks for the same test again after at least 90 days.
insights.do: Ask your doctor to repeat creatinine, eGFR and urine albumin at least 90 days after 9 Oct 2026.
insights.expected: Two results 90 or more days apart show whether the change is lasting and how fast it is moving.

insights.title: Your 2- and 5-year kidney failure risk was calculated
insights.found: With your age, sex, eGFR and urine albumin, the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (4-variable) gives 1.9% at 2 years and 7.2% at 5 years.
insights.why: Your eGFR is below 60, the range the equation was built for, and every input it needs was measured.
insights.means: Most people with these numbers do not reach kidney failure in 5 years. The equation was validated internationally but has not been recalibrated for people in India, so read it as approximate.
insights.do: Use it as a starting point with your doctor, not a forecast. It is recalculated each time your kidney tests are repeated.
insights.expected: A falling risk on repeat tests is the sign that matters.

insights.title: One blood pressure reading was above 140
insights.found: Your office systolic blood pressure on 9 Oct 2026 was 146 mmHg.
insights.why: Our rule flags a systolic reading of 140 or more, and you take telmisartan and amlodipine.
insights.means: A single office reading does not diagnose anything. Repeated readings, preferably outside the clinic, show your usual blood pressure.
insights.do: Take repeat readings within 1 to 8 weeks (our analysis retest window), at home if you can, and share them with your doctor.
insights.expected: A set of readings tells your doctor whether your current medicines are enough.
insights.helps: Several readings give a truer picture than one.

insights.title: Your potassium was just above the lab's range
insights.found: Potassium 5.3 mmol/L on 9 Oct 2026; the lab's range is 3.5-5.1.
insights.why: Potassium is balanced by the kidneys, and your kidney function is reduced.
insights.means: A small rise like this needs your doctor to look at it together with your kidney results and medicines. No rule in our library reads potassium on its own.
insights.do: Ask your doctor about this result at your next visit; do not change medicines yourself.
insights.expected: Your doctor decides whether to repeat it and when.

insights.title: Your haemoglobin is below the usual range for men
insights.why: It is below 13.5 g/dL, the fifth centile of healthy men in our rule's source.
insights.means: That boundary describes a population; it is not a decision point. The useful question is whether iron is low, and if so, why.
insights.do: Ask your doctor whether iron studies are needed.
insights.expected: Iron studies show whether there is a cause to treat.

insights.title: Your blood sugar is in the 'prediabetes' band
insights.found: Fasting glucose 101 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L) and HbA1c 5.8% on 9 Oct 2026.
insights.why: Both fall in the impaired-fasting-glucose and 5.7-6.4% HbA1c bands.
insights.means: This is a risk state, not diabetes. In the source cohort about a third of people in this band returned to normal. In Asian Indians the HbA1c cut-off misses some people, so a glucose tolerance test is the more sensitive check if your doctor suspects more.
insights.do: Recheck fasting glucose and HbA1c in 6 to 12 months.
insights.expected: A repeat shows whether you are moving towards or away from diabetes.

insights.title: Your urate is above the definition of high urate
insights.found: Serum urate 8.4 mg/dL on 9 Oct 2026. You take febuxostat.
insights.why: Our rule flags urate above the boundary for asymptomatic high urate in men.
insights.means: The review behind this rule found no clear benefit from urate-lowering treatment when there are no symptoms, and advises managing heart risk factors on their own merits. Your record does not say why febuxostat was started.
insights.do: Keep taking febuxostat unless your doctor says otherwise, and ask what it is for in your case.
insights.expected: A clear reason for each medicine makes the next review simpler.

ask.a: Your eGFR was 41 on 9 Oct 2026, which is stage G3b, and your urine albumin was 420 mg/g, far above the lab's limit of 30. The Kidney Failure Risk Equation puts your risk of kidney failure at 1.9% over 2 years and 7.2% over 5 years. A repeat test at least 90 days after the first shows whether this is lasting.
eGFR estimates how well your kidneys filter blood, from your creatinine, age and sex. Yours was 41; the lab's healthy range starts at 90.

ask.q: What does albumin in my urine mean?
ask.a: Albumin is a protein that healthy kidneys keep in the blood. Your urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio was 420 mg/g; the lab's limit is below 30. It is also one of the four inputs to your kidney failure risk.

ask.q: What is my kidney failure risk?
ask.a: 1.9% at 2 years and 7.2% at 5 years, from the 4-variable Kidney Failure Risk Equation. It has not been recalibrated for people in India, so treat it as approximate.

ask.q: Is my blood pressure too high?
ask.a: One office reading was 146 systolic, above 140. One reading cannot diagnose anything; repeat readings, ideally at home, over the next 1 to 8 weeks will show your usual level.
Your record codes no diabetes. Fasting glucose 101 mg/dL and HbA1c 5.8% are in the prediabetes band, a risk state. About a third of people in this band return to normal. Recheck in 6 to 12 months.
Your haemoglobin was 11.6 g/dL, below the usual range for men. The run cannot tell why. Iron studies are the next step to see whether iron is low.

No - never stop a medicine on your own. Your urate was 8.4 mg/dL. The evidence behind our rule finds no clear benefit from urate-lowering treatment when there are no symptoms, but your record does not say why febuxostat was started. Ask your doctor.
It was 5.3 mmol/L, just above the lab's range of 3.5-5.1. Your doctor should look at it alongside your kidney results and medicines; no rule in our library reads potassium on its own.
Not calculated. PhenoAge needs nine blood results and 7 are missing: albumin, CRP, lymphocyte %, MCV, RDW, alkaline phosphatase and white cell count. We never estimate it from missing values.

ask.q: What did the drug discovery research find?
ask.a: It found 25 biological targets (the portal lists the first 12) linked to your record, including genes tied to kidney disease and blood sugar, and profiled 730 known compounds against them. No docking was run. This is research, not treatment.

Repeat kidney function, potassium and urine albumin at least 90 days after October; repeat blood pressure; a full blood count with iron studies; and a first cholesterol panel so heart-risk models can run.

glossary: Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
A waste product from muscle, cleared by the kidneys; used to estimate kidney function.
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio: how much protein (albumin) leaks into the urine.
Kidney Failure Risk Equation: the chance of needing dialysis or a transplant within 2 or 5 years, for people with an eGFR below 60.
A blood salt needed for nerves, muscles and heart rhythm; the kidneys keep it in balance.
The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
Average blood sugar over about the last 2-3 months.
Uric acid in the blood. High levels can form crystals in joints (gout).
One of our clinical checks. Each has a source, a threshold and an evidence grade; it fires only when your result clears it.

genes.function: Electrogenic Na(+)-coupled sugar symporter that actively transports D-glucose at the plasma membrane, with a Na(+) to sugar coupling ratio of 1:1.
Receptor for both mineralocorticoids (MC) such as aldosterone and glucocorticoids (GC) such as corticosterone or cortisol.
Receptor for angiotensin II, a vasoconstricting peptide, which acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and sodium retention by the kidney.
Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen.
PPIase that catalyzes the cis-trans isomerization of proline imidic peptide bonds in oligopeptides and may therefore assist protein folding.

Metabolic-stress sensing protein kinase that phosphorylates the alpha subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha) in response to various stress, such as unfolded protein response (UPR).
Deacetylates a wide range of non-histone substrates.
G protein-coupled receptor for glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1).
Cell surface glycoprotein receptor involved in the costimulatory signal essential for T-cell receptor (TCR)-mediated T-cell activation.
